utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So two days after you say that Karadzic told you in a one-on-one meeting that they should all be killed, you receive two decisions in writing that show exactly what Karadzic ordered you to do.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but I would just like to ask you, Mr. Tapuskovic, not to take words out of context. I did not say that he only said they all need to be killed. He added a great deal of explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were talking about civilians, and I explained all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, look at this paragraph 199, 206, and 209. We are still on the first subject. In paragraph 199, we can see that on the same day you had a completely normal conversation with no interference at all with Karadzic when he told you -- you say: "He called me, and he wanted to know what's going on with the transport of civilians. I told him that more than a half of those people were loaded onto buses and that I expect that the transport would be completed by the end of the day."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now look at paragraph 206 and later 209. Paragraph 206, you mentioned that Karadzic told you a man would come with instructions as to Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 29771 to 29784. what you should do. And in paragraph 208, towards the end, you say verbatim: "I assumed that he, the man who introduced himself as Beara, was the one sent by Karadzic." And as you say in paragraph 209, he was the one who told you everyone should be killed.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We saw yesterday that transcript of that intercept. Just tell me one thing. That transcript of the intercept, it was done on the basis of what? Did you listen to the audio first and then wrote it down? How was the transcript made? Why are you looking towards the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me? It was not I who made the transcript. I thought you were asking the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you. How was the transcript made? Did you listen to that conversation and then wrote it down, or did you just receive it, this paper, as it was presented here?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only got the paper. I don't know how it was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On this piece of paper that we all have in front of us, it is never alleged that the conversation included a phrase like "a man would come bringing instructions" as to what you should do.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, I explained this to my lawyers. I gave my statement because -- before this paper was shown to me, and I established that it was the way it was. The Prosecutor warned me that this piece of paper did not contain this phrase. I said I remembered it clearly, that they should check the recording, and they informed me later that they listened to the recording, it was full of interference, and this part was not audible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of March, 2003, I was given a transcript of an interview of Mr. Ruez with Deronjic on Variants A and B, and out of the wealth of this material containing several hundred pages, I singled out two or three. I talked to the Prosecutor yesterday and asked them to provide this in English. The Prosecutor has this part of the interview, and I wanted us to see what this witness told the investigator at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It was an interview -- interpreter's correction -- from 1990. The interpreter is not sure which year Mr. Tapuskovic mentioned, the date of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really believe this is an important issue. Let us clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Can you clarify the year of the interview, which wasn't plain to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I mentioned it. 12th March 2003 -- 2001. Sorry. 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please pay attention, pay special attention to page 6, lines 1 to 10. It says that there was a telegram, and it says then -- it was a telegram, a wire that was forwarded on the 13th of July, 1995, the same day when he talked to Karadzic in the morning. It says: "You are not talking directly to the president, you are talking through a mediator." And then Mr. Deronjic answers: "But you can't hear this?" "No. I'm talking directly to the president."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have difficulty locating the relevant passage. Could you help us?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- line 9, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So the first question is we're talking about a telegram. It seems to be an intercept on 13th of July, 1995. What is more important, throughout this conversation you never mentioned that a man would come bringing instructions. Neither here nor in another conversation that I can't present to the Court now, you mentioned that there would be a man coming with instructions or anything about this Beara. Can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I regret not having this paper in front of me in Serbian, and I don't know what it relates to, but I will answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it relates precisely to the subject of our discussion, this conversation that we have transcribed here.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what it relates to, but I cannot find my complete answer in this paper I have, but I don't doubt that what you are saying is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask Your Honours to allow me to tender this. I don't have time to deal with all of this, but it is clear that he is not communicating with Karadzic directly. On the contrary, he is warned many times that's talking through someone else. It seems to be an operative officer of the Bratunac Brigade. That's one. And second, there is no reference to that particular phrase we are talking about. I would like to tender this into evidence because it shows clearly what I am arguing. There is no reference at all to a man who is supposed to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How can you explain this to the Judges? How come you didn't mention it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, Mr. Tapuskovic, do you know the circumstances under which I gave my statement? At that moment, there was no indictment against me, and I was certainly not motivated to indict myself. I told the Office of the Prosecutor that all my conversations were recorded, intercepted, and many of them were analysed in the General Staff of the army of Yugoslavia. I told them that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But tell the Judges one more thing. Did this telegram exist at the time? It was a -- was it an intercept that you were able to analyse? Is that something you said in your statement of 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you talking about? What intercept? What document? Can you specify?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Before the investigative organs, that is the investigators of this Tribunal, the investigator showed you a communication between you and Karadzic that was not direct at any point in time. There was always a mediator, and you were always being told what Karadzic had said. You were not able to have a single direct contact with Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must be his version. I don't know whether or not I spoke to him directly. I told the Prosecutor here that at one point I heard Karadzic directly. I heard his voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you are saying this here for the first time. At the time when you were shown this document from this transcript of the conversation, there is no single reference to this man, and in 2001, you didn't mention him either. You didn't say that a man was coming.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, but I explained why I failed to mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look now at paragraph 182. But before that, would you be so kind as to answer one other question. Before the 1st of July, in the area where all this took place in Srebrenica, first of all, was it a demilitarised zone?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You talked about it yesterday. Were there incidents originating from the Muslim side targeting Serbian villages, and were Serbian villages even burned in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now look at paragraph 182. You say: "Sinisa Glogovac and I spent the night together with the soldiers between the 10th and the 11th in an area called Divljakinje. On the 11th in the morning we went again to Pribicevac, to the plateau where the forward command post was located." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me now, at the moment when you were on that location, did the UNPROFOR forces react? Was fire opened by the UNPROFOR forces against the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, not shelling. Was there any fire before that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Then you go on to say, "At one point rumours circulated that Mladic had arrived. We saw him on that plateau about ten metres away from us. He was upset, angry, and he was yelling. Glogovac and I were standing about ten, 15 metres away to the side."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 183 you say: "They were in a lot of hurry. There was a lot of commotion, and it was very hectic. I soon realised what the reason was. Mladic got into a car and set off towards a place called Kvarc where there was some sort of transmitter, a radio relay. Ten metres or so after, the planes started flying over that area, bombing the positions, and I realised that Mladic was upset and angry precisely about this. Very soon after that, some bombs were dropped very close to us. There were two aircraft. Two sorties were made. It was over very soon." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Muslim fighters, even though they had air support, did not defend Srebrenica at all? They moved elsewhere, leaving civilians behind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first there was fighting between Muslims and Serbs. They left later, on the 11th, leaving civilians behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And just one more paragraph. Paragraph 184. Correction, 144. You spoke here about state security. You talked about the gathering of intelligence. You said there was a lot of activity going on related to intelligence affairs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in that area were all sorts of intelligence officers active from all states, all countries?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If there was so much intelligence activity, so many representatives of the press and the media, does it make sense to you that some sort of operation can be started in the presence of the UNPROFOR if that operation ended as we know it ended?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just the last question: Was there any official representative of the army of Yugoslavia in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered this question many times. As far as I know, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, it is time to adjourn. Are you going to be fairly brief or --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to strike a balance between what I should and what I must ask in order to be brief, but after the adjournment would be more helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will make it after the adjournment. There were various documents which Mr. Tapuskovic put in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Two decisions which seem to me to be admissible if he wants. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No objection to those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Part of an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I don't understand the relevance of that at this stage. It seems to me that the passage being -- the intercept being referred to by the interviewing investigator is the very intercept that we've got. I haven't been able to check every line of it. Therefore, if that's the purpose for which it's being put in, it's mere duplication of our exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I took it to be the fact that the witness did not refer to speaking to via an intermediary or speaking directly to Karadzic and he didn't mention these other two things, and he's given an answer as to why he didn't, so I think technically that's admissible too. What weight it has, of course, is a matter entirely for the Trial Chamber. The sensible thing might be to give those C numbers, Court numbers, beginning with the order. I don't know if the registry have got these. We've got an order of the -- yes, the appointment, I suppose, would be the one. It's headed "Decision." It's dated the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Court Exhibit 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Next the order. It's headed "Order." The same day.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Court Exhibit 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And the extract from the interview with the investigator.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Court Exhibit 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'd be grateful if it could be confirmed that the date, the last date we had was the 12th of March of 2001. It might be helpful to have the correct date for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, apparently it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now. Half an hour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, a few matters. First the intercept that's covered in your statement at paragraph 206. If you want to turn that up, please. And we now know from the Court Exhibit number 23, which you don't have Serbian or B/C/S, it only being in English as produced, I think, that you were interviewed about this topic, and the interviewers asked you about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a copy. Perhaps I could provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we have it in Serbian too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's clear that you were interviewed about this intercept, whether or not it was shown to you. And in the course of that, it was made clear that the communications were by a middleman. Do you recall that fact in the interview?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In your statement at page 206 -- paragraph 206, before you'd been shown the transcript of the intercept, you gave an account of what was said to you, and you said at the end, "I don't remember whether these words were uttered by him or an intermediary."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You were then shown here a couple of days ago our Exhibit 601, the transcript itself, which has a break in it indicative of non-continuous transcript, or intercept, but which nevertheless contains no reference to your speaking directly to Karadzic but speaking to the intermediary; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of what I see here in front of me, it seems evident that I am talking about the middleman and to the middleman and that he is involved in the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In giving evidence to the learned Judges yesterday, you spoke of the transcript being incomplete because things were said that were not recorded there or not heard there.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And in paragraph 206 of your witness statement, you refer to the passage of the conversation where you were told that someone would come with instructions, and we can see that that is not reflected on the transcript Exhibit 601.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Does it remain your evidence that in this same telephone discussion which is the subject of this transcript, there were things said that are not recorded there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I abide by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now dealing with the emissary that you say it was Beara, expecting someone to come, apart from Beara, did anyone else turn up, saying he'd come from Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not know Mr. Beara, and I did not know who could come. When he showed up in my office, I assumed that he was the man who came after my conversation with Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he hold himself out by manner or by what he said as having some authority? The accused has suggested he was just a man on a sort of drunken frolic, or something to that effect. Did he, so far as you're concerned, indicate any authority in his mission?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice says that the accused suggested that he was some type of alcoholic. I did not suggest anything. I just quoted what Mr. Deronjic wrote in his statement, that Beara, that is to say this man who came, was tipsy. Quoted him. I cannot suggest that Beara was an alcoholic or was not an alcoholic because I don't know the man at all. I just quoted from the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We have the point. Perhaps you'd like to repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. And I have a recollection that I'll turn up in due course, the way the accused asked the question, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think it matters very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did Beara hold himself out, by either his manner or by what he said, as having authority to give you instructions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall answer that question. It is correct that at that moment he looked quite tipsy. That was the word I used, and that is what the witnesses say, those who saw him that night in my office. So it was that he was under the influence of a certain dose of alcohol. I don't want to deny that. He did behave like a man with a degree of authority. He held a high rank at that time in the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You've been asked various things about the circumstances in which you pleaded guilty and the terms upon which you did so. I'm sure the Chamber is alive to this but the precise terms upon which you've pleaded guilty are set out in something called the factual basis of your plea, which is the third part of the bundle, and at page numbered 406 in the top right-hand corner and starting at about paragraph 30, the Chamber can find the terms, the factual basis for which you pleaded guilty; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is completely correct. All the precise terms and conditions were specified, those under which I pleaded guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Turning now to what you set out at paragraph 63 in your statement, on the pattern of events and the use of volunteers, the accused has suggested that you brought these volunteers in yourself for your own purposes. In your statement, you indicate that what happened in your town happened in other locations and in a regular way, so as to justify the phrase or the word "pattern". Two questions -- three questions. Did you have access to volunteers of the kind you describe whom you could command?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. I did not know them, and never was I in contact with these volunteers, including at the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would there have been any purpose in volunteers coming into your town and acting in the way you describe? I mean, any purpose that you would have approved of or agreed with?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of their coming to Bratunac, the way I understood things, was to take over Bratunac, to have Bratunac taken over by the Serbs. They did not fully exercise power at that time in Bratunac, they only participated in the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was that something you wanted done in that way, by that form of violence, or not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I explained the way in which I thought that Variants A and B should be carried out, and there are records of that in the Office of the Prosecutor. I was present during these events, and I precisely described my own participation in all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And then the last question on this topic and then just a couple more topics. The last question on this topic: You speak of this pattern having been repeated in other locations. Can you give us an approximate idea of how many other locations you saw this pattern being repeated?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Due to the circumstances in Bratunac, I was not in a position to closely monitor events in neighbouring municipalities, but I do know about them from the period that followed afterwards. Of course I did know about some things because we were so nearby, and I'm talking about April, precisely Zvornik, which is 43 kilometres away from Bratunac. Of course I was aware of what happened in Bijeljina too, which started a bit earlier. As for the way in which this evolved and the purpose involved, I learnt of all of that gradually. I had quite a bit of information, though, when these events were actually taking place. I also knew what was going on in Visegrad. I read the newspapers and saw what was happening in Banja Luka, and I described that in what I had to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two more questions about weapons and arming. The accused has drawn to your attention that one of the places from which you say arms were coming, Tuzla, was a predominantly Muslim town. Can you explain, if it needs explanation, how it would be possible for arms for Serbs to come from Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I going to tell you what my assumption is. As far as I know and as far as I was told, weapons were obtained on several occasions. Goran Zekic went up there with those people through the military. I assume that this was done secretly and that of course some other services in this town could not have been aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The accused used the word "smuggling" for the movement of arms into Bosnia. Smuggling -- well, so far as you're concerned, was the activity, whether described as smuggling or not, done with the approval of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described the participation of particular organs and persons from these organs in such events. I would not like to draw a general conclusion, but it is obvious that some organs and some persons from these organs, including the army, the police, and the Territorial Defence, were taking part in such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And you've spoken of Kertes and his location in the same building as occupied by the accused. Kertes offered you an opportunity to meet the accused. You make it clear you don't know whether he was able to deliver on that offer, but you declined the offer?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I declined. Goran Zekic also declined the offer. We probably did so for different reasons, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And in a word, your reason?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reason were my activities aimed against the authorities and the policy that was advocated by Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nothing else in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it. As far as this trial is concerned, you are now free to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: While the witness is leaving, Mr. Nice, could you help us about Tuesday's witness or witnesses? It might be helpful to have a statement of those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you haven't had one so far, I'll ensure that it comes your way if we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be we've had one, but a 92 bis application.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I expect you have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 89(F) statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: An 89(F) statement. Yes. For the first witness, I understand that an 89(F) is required. We'll make one available. I'll go and deal with it straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is the order of the witnesses the one that was provided in the general review for next week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps to make sure that it's clarified you would just give us the order verbally again since we've got two orders now. They may be the same, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We'll have to go into private session if I am to give the names. Can you just give me one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we're in --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I take it the witness is on his way.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next witness is the witness C-057. He's a protected witness with voice and image distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Witness C-057, you gave a statement to an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor in July this year. Was it taken in the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, that statement was taken in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review this document while in The Hague and preparing for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, I had the opportunity of reviewing it in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: During the preparation of your -- for your testimony, did you, together with Prosecution staff, go through each and every paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, each and every paragraph was dealt with in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you identify, while doing so, a few minor errors such as two incorrect dates and a few unclear English expressions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. That was noticed and corrections were made or, rather, amendments were made to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, while doing this we actually prepared an addendum to the statement with some minor corrections and clarifications, and the Prosecution would like to tender both documents. But before I do that --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you have opportunity to review and sign this addendum on the 25th of November, 2003?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. I reviewed this addendum and signed it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Are both your statement from July this year and the addendum true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: They are absolutely accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would like to tender both documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are apparently told we're short a pseudonym sheet, but it may be that it's been suggested that it's in the page of the statement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the point. The name of the witness is on the -- in the statement, and all his personal details. So I felt there's no need to have a pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 607, Your Honours. I believe that's -- tab 1 is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not intend to go into any of the details of the statement or the addendum. All I intend to do is to address a few of the exhibits that are going in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would so that we know and the accused should know what they are, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Just clarification: The documents tab 2 to tab 9 were actually provided by the witness himself, and they are all addressed in detail in the statement that is already tendered, and I do not want to go with the witness through all these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Just this question, sir: Did you provide, while giving your initial statement, a lot of documents that deal with your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. Along with the statement, I submitted a certain number of documents that I had, ones that I kept, and that was done in the month of July when I made my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can the tab 4 be put to the witness. Tab 4 is a marching order from the 1st of July, 1991. It's actually a document consisting of a warning order and then the order for march.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, did you provide these -- these pages, these two documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. I provided these two documents to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On page 2 or, actually, the marching order as such, in the first paragraph reference is made - in the first line, actually, of paragraph 1 - reference to made to the internal enemy aided by external factors. Could you explain who the internal enemy was at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: At that time, the internal enemy were the secessionist forces, as is said here, primarily in Croatia and Slovenia. So that is what is basically meant, the secessionist forces. In everyday conversations, we used the word "Ustasha forces" in respect of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In that same paragraph there is also mentioned the task that you were assigned to or the troops that were involved in this marching order, and there is a reference to preventing clashes and the same is also mentioned in the next paragraph where is mention of preventing inter-ethnic clashes in the Vukovar section. Is that actually what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: This was the official order. I can only give a comment. This is a document. In practice we were cautioned that actually it was the Ustasha forces that were the enemy, that we would have major problems over there on the other side, and I think that I mentioned that in my statement. We were cautioned that the entire population in Croatian settlements had an Ustasha orientation and that even pets and domestic animals had an Ustasha orientation. So this order is worded nicely but the practical instructions were quite different.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you reached the territory of Croatia, did you actually prevent inter-ethnic clashes and serve as a buffer or did you do something different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No, we did not serve as a buffer. In practice we are launching an attack against the territory and the Croatian population fled from the areas where we came, so we did not serve as a buffer.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mention in your statement and you mention it also today that there was actually a quite different oral order accompanying this -- this written order. Was this something unusual or was it a common occurrence in the JNA at that time to have conflicting or absolutely different written and oral orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: It happened even in peacetime and also then. As it can be seen, the orders were in proper form, but in practice things collided with these orders. What was said were things that were inappropriate to be put in an order, and I mentioned that in the previous example, that things that were said to us were different from what was written in the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In paragraph 5 of this same marching order in relation to the tank company, there is a reference that the tank company should avoid all provocations and open fire in self-defence. Did the JNA indeed operate in Croatia firing only in self-defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No. No. Things turned out quite differently in relation to what is stated here. An attack was launched a month later, but it was absolutely not in self-defence, not in self-defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the paragraphs 5.a, 5.b, and 5.c related to the task of the various units, there is reference, quite the similar one in all these paragraphs, speaking of "during the march be ready to break up relatively powerful forces in sectors with major populated areas." Were you given any concrete instruction how to break up resistance in populated areas, in particular in relation to the civilians that were in these areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Well, the oral instruction was to open fire by all means, that we should not sustain any losses whatsoever. And what was expected was large concentrations of the MUP in towns with a predominantly Croatian population. So what we were supposed to do was to prevent any attempt of an attack at us.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This is enough from this document. The next document I briefly want to address with you is tab 5. It is again a marching and defend order of the 27th of July, 1991. And just have a look in the first paragraph. It says here: "Early in the morning on the 27th July, 1991, a conflict broke out between the Serbian population and Croatian MUP forces in the village of Erdut." To your knowledge, did such a conflict between the population and the Croatian MUP indeed break out or what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No. I know about this. This paragraph is inaccurate. There was no conflict. There was no clash between the MUP and the forces of Serb ethnicity. This order was issued because we were shelling Erdut a day or two prior to that in the evening in an area where MUP was concentrated. It is not true that there was a clash between Serbs and Croats on that territory. What is true is that we shelled the MUP forces in Erdut and its surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And now tab 7. Tab 7 is a newspaper article provided by you, and in this newspaper article there is actually a reference to a long battle in Erdut. First of all, did you yourself speak with journalists about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No, I did not speak to journalists about it. Somebody from the command, I suppose, brought journalists to our position, introduced me, and the journalist took my photograph. I made no comment, I was only photographed. I think you can see the contents of this article and the occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next exhibit that I want briefly to address with you is tab 10, consisting of three charts, and my question to you first is: Did you prepare, during your proofing session together with Prosecution staff, these organigrammes of the units you were involved with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. I prepared these myself. These are accurate organigrammes of the units where I served. These are accurate schemes indicating composition, strength, et cetera, weaponry as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to the organigramme attack on Luzac, if you would please have a look at this, you have indicated here the Novi Sad Corps on top of it and, below, your brigade command. How and if -- did those two organs work together during the attack; and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: These two bodies did work together. At the silo, an operative command was set up consisting of a part of commanding officers from the Novi Sad Corps and part of the commanding officers from my brigade. So they functioned as one joint operative body.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: During the proofing, did you also review a document -- photos related to weaponry and aircraft involved in the battles that you were engaged with?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be tab 11.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did look at those photographs. They depict the weaponry and equipment that were at the disposal of my unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibits tab 1 to tab 10 need to be under seal, the others not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, were you also shown -- tab 13, please. Were you also shown a report from a security organ dated the 1st of October, 1991? Did you have time to review this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. I reviewed this document a couple of days ago. I'm aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was this the first time that you saw this document or --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did I -- I don't have tab 13. The last tab in the binder I received is 12. Perhaps Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff was wrong about the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll make sure you get a copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic actually has a copy. He got it yesterday, but the tabs are obviously not in order in relation to tab 13 and tab 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That can be done in due course. He's got a copy now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see this document from the 1st of October, 1991, before or is that the first time that you saw it in the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I saw this document in the Office of the Prosecutor for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Looking at the stamps at the top and the end of this document, does it appear to you that it is authentic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: The document is obviously authentic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the text, it refers to Arkan's behaviour in the field, and you yourself, in your statement, gave a lot of similar facts as to Arkan's behaviour in the field. Can you comment on what is described here in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I don't think there's any need for me to read the document now. All that is written here is absolutely accurate. At the time when this information was received, I had not met him yet, but all the commanding officers said that he should be given a wide berth because he treated all of the officers of the JNA very badly. I only had occasion to see him for the first time when the church was destroyed. It was later, towards the end of the month indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In this document, we have here a suggestion at the end from the person who signs it, and it says here: "We suggest immediate measures to be taken against Arkan so the JNA could distance itself from his operations which have negative influence on the morale of the JNA members in that area." Are you aware whether any measures were indeed taken against Arkan and his men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I do know no measures were taken. In fact, measures were taken to the opposite effect. Arkan reinforced his position, and he was untouchable on this ground, in this area, as far as his troops were concerned. If any measures were taken, they were completely to the contrary. That is, measures were taken to reinforce his position.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And finally, tab 14. Can they please be shown to the witness. It's another report of the security organ dealing with Arkan from the 18th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you have opportunity to review this document during the proofing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The format of the document, in particular the stamps at the beginning and the end, would you say it's authentic or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: This is, in my view, absolutely authentic, certainly authentic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In this document, referring to the training centre in particular and also a reference is in here in the last sentence in relation to the media who, according to these findings of the person who drafted the document, gave a lot of publicity to this behaviour. Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I can give you a brief comment. It was television at that time which started making a hero out of him, ascribing great credit and merits to him in terms of struggle for Serbian freedom. We knew that in practice, in reality, things were quite different, but in the media he was depicted as a hero.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And finally, Your Honours, just for this testimony, as a help, the witness did produce a map. It's actually based on Exhibit 326, tab 15. He just highlighted the locations in which he was present. And that concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. But I would like to make one remark. The witness, of course, is anxious that his identity is not revealed, and the point is during the cross-examination, there should not be any reference to the names of his battalion, his units. That should be -- that should not be mentioned. It would be enough to speak of brigade, battalion, and company. His superiors should not be mentioned by name. It could be easily done by referring to "the person mentioned in paragraph so-and-so." And finally, all private matters, and the actions, the concrete actions of the witness in the field should not be mentioned or should then -- or we should move into private session for these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, in advance, Mr. May, how much time will I have with this witness, because in the schedule I received, it said three hours. I just want to know in advance. I don't want you to tell me that towards the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That schedule is merely an overall estimate by the Prosecution. We had in mind an hour and a half to two hours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to be more efficient in the use of my time, I will first focus, Mr. C-057, on these several exhibits that have been tendered. This marching order, as far as I can see, relates -- first an explanation: "Enemy forces with the aid of outside factors have been causing ethnic conflicts for some time now with the objective of toppling the legitimate authorities." And then it goes on to say that, "These activities are the most intensive in the territories of the Republics of Slovenia and Croatia, and particular hotbeds are Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and Krajina." Was it true at the time that particular hotbeds were located in the territory of Slovenia and Croatia and that there was already talk of the secession of these republics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. It was already the time when there were even armed clashes. As far as I remember, on the 4th of May there was a clash with the members of the MUP of Croatia and the residents of Borovo Selo, Borovo village. Before that, there already had been armed clashes around the Catholic Easter. So you can well say that those were hotbeds of crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But what it says in the order is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. Those were hotbeds of crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says: "For the time being, the JNA has with great effort, without the use of force, been successfully executing its tasks in preventing clashes of major scale." It says specifically in this document "with great effort and without the use of force." I suppose that too is correct. The JNA tried to prevent all this without resorting to force. Is that true or not, Mr. C-057?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I cannot give you a definitive answer because I did not go there at the time. I only went there on the 1st of August. So I cannot tell you exactly whether it is completely accurate or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. C-057, I asked you a question. I got an answer. Thank you. The next thing it says: "Members of the JNA and their families have been subjected to great pressures by slights and provocations, all intended to make members of the army resort to armed force so that the army as a whole might be presented as an aggressive factor." Are you aware of this? Is it true that JNA members and their families were subjected to major pressure through slurs, slights, humiliations, et cetera. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No, I'm not, because at the time I was in Serbia where we were not, of course, subjected to any pressure or humiliation. I simply wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were not informed of what was going on at the time in Croatia and Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I don't remember anyone speaking to me about that in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, it says that that unit received an assignment to go on the 30th of March on a march in a single file, and it says the axis was Zrenjanin, Aradac village, Zabalj, Belgrade-Novi Sad road junction, Beska village, Indjija village, Putinci, Ruma, Radinci, towards the area of Vukovar; and then it goes on to say: "Their objective is to secure the unhindered and unconditional execution of tasks geared at preventing inter-ethnic conflict in the area of Vukovar-Vinkovci." That is how the order reads.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: That's true. I read the order, I am aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were an officer of the JNA then. You read the order. Tell me one thing. I suppose that the order is made known to the entire unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: That's true. All members of the unit, all subordinates, are informed of the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it read out to the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No, it isn't. Based on that order, I wrote my own marching order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the subordinate commander writes his own order in keeping with the superior order. They have to coincide.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: That's correct. I gave my own order in keeping with the order I received, with the proviso that I cautioned my subordinate officers of the -- the oral information I had been given, that we would fare very badly because all the local population was pro-Ustashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We'll come back to that later, C-057. I'm discussing this document now which is an exhibit. What you are saying now is not written in the order.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Of course it is not written. I'm telling you what I was told verbally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says, in 5.a: "Be ready during the march to break up stronger forces in areas of major populated places." When they say stronger forces, they mean strong armed units that could be hostile to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. It means armed units that could attack us. I don't see anything that could give rise to any doubts here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I want everything to be clear. I don't want any confusion or misunderstandings, such as your unit going to attack populated areas. It says: "Stronger units in major populated areas." It means units that could attack you; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Of course that's what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In 5.b, it says: "Open fire during the march only in self-defence and upon my permission. Do not allow any provocation or firing in response to provocation." That means you are allowed to open fire only in response to attack, and do not allow provocations or response to provocations.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: That's what I said to my subordinates. Do not open fire in case fire is -- tomatoes are thrown at us or something stupid like that, something trivial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'll skip one part. A morale -- morale and psychological support. It says: "Immediately hold meetings of military staff where attention should be drawn to the significance of the tasks ahead and possible forms of provocation, how to act in such circumstances and what measures to undertake." This order refers to the arrival of your unit in the Vukovar-Vinkovci sector with clearly designated tasks to prevent inter-ethnic conflict in that region. And it refers to how the units should behave in keeping with this order; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, the next exhibit is marching order dated 27 July. It says: "On the 27th of July, there was a conflict between the Serbian population and Croatian MUP forces in the village of Erdut and its broader area." And in paragraph 2, it says: "Upon emerging at the destination of the march, use combat formation to separate the parties, that is the opposed sides, along the Novi-Erdut, trig point 1.58 line. That is, effect their separation." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: That's what the order says. There was no conflict. The occasion for that order was our shelling of the Erdut area, the Erdut tower, and that entire locality. So there was no conflict between the Serb and the Croatian population. It was us who shelled this area the day before. We shelled the localities where Croatian MUP forces were concentrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were supposed to go in and separate their forces from the other part where the civilian population was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No. When we came in on the 1st of August, those forces fled before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you had no one to separate. They simply fled before you came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 5, it says: "Open fire only if the unit is attacked." And that is reiterated in relation to each of the units named here. Then it says that the minesweeper should be kept ready to remove minefields. Do you remember the removal of minefields, the clearing of minefields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I don't remember it. There was no clearing of minefields. I did that as part of the assignment of the advanced unit. I didn't open fire on those who were fleeing. I saw them on a couple of occasions. They were fleeing and there was -- there were no mines so we had nothing to remove.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't fire even at armed units that were fleeing before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 6.3 says: "The focus of security should be protection from surprise fire and fire opened from ambushes. During action, strictly respect the provisions of the Geneva Conventions. Gather weapons captured and surrendered in one place and upon completion of the task hand them over to the --" what follows is illegible, but I suppose -- yes, it's "military police company." Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I don't have the document in front of me but I believe your quotation is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking this because that is what it is supposed to mean, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, and that's how we acted in these situations. If you want my comment on what you just said, there was no captured weaponry. We didn't seize any weapons and we didn't capture any prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The order says that you should act in every way in accordance with the Geneva Conventions. That is a rule that you must have been familiar with as a trained officer of the JNA and during your training in the JNA you must have been made aware of the rules of the Geneva Convention and what such warnings mean. Correct, Mr. C-057?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The Geneva Conventions, the customs and laws of war are referred to. Well, not referred to, they are studied at the military academy in detail. Unfortunately, later, in operations that followed, this was not mentioned and there were grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No doubt about that. I'm just looking at this particular exhibit, and I'm saying that the command that issues this order, and Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff drew my attention to the fact that I should not mention who the commander is or anything else, so the commander who is issuing this order is the lieutenant colonel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, I know who this is. There is no need to mention his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, so this is not some kind of a general order of the Supreme Command. This is the order of a lieutenant colonel that you are subordinated to. In his order, he also makes it clear that you should act in accordance with the Geneva Conventions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: That was readily understood. And not only that, it was his duty to put this into the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This newspaper article was also given as an exhibit, and it is considered to be some kind of propaganda. What is said here is that there is this fort --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us -- if we are going to talk about the article, it may be sensible to go into private session to do so. Go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. C-057, Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff showed you some diagrams here, ones that you made yourself, and you confirmed that that is the way things were. And then here it says on the diagram -- she just commented on it superficially, but I would like to hear your brief comment. Attack on Luzac. What kind of attack was this? What is Luzac? Where is Luzac and what kind of attack was this on Luzac? But please try to keep it as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Luzac is a settlement, a very small village to the north of Vukovar and to the south of Borovo Kombinac [phoen] on the banks of the Danube, like Vukovar. The attack on Luzac was planned by the command to cut through the forces of the MUP and the ZNG from Borovo Naselje and Vukovar, that is to say, to separate the two, to cut through them. That was the basic aim of the attack that was carried out on the 1st of November. I don't know whether I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So was there a conflict there between these forces and the forces of the National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. That morning, we had a conflict. We had sustained losses. I don't know what else I should say. Of course there was a conflict. The conflicts went on until the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you sustained losses, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: The initial losses, my initial losses that morning were ten or 11 wounded that morning, but my losses went up to 27 killed and wounded persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that only within your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Only within the company that I commanded, a reinforced company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Only a reinforced company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. Considerable losses, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So these forces were rather powerful, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No. No. It doesn't mean that they were powerful. They were well organised, well organised. It's called flexible defence. I don't know how familiar you are with military terminology. Rapid gunfire, losses sustained by the enemy, and then quickly withdraw to shelters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to explain this diagram. You talk about a unit. Now I have to find the right way of putting this without identifying you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Well, just say what you have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it's a brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The attack on Luzac. I'm not going to read the actual names out or anything else. And then there is the command of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not naming any names. Then under that command, you have one mechanised company; is that right? Motorised company. Please take a look at this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could somebody please assist me with this? Could somebody find the document for me?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's tab 10, the third chart.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, what is it you want to know in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just a brief description of the boxes that you placed here. As far as I can understand, under the command of the brigade you have one MC. That is probably the first motorised company or something like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I think it would be good to go into private session very briefly, just for five minutes, then I can properly explain this, otherwise I don't think I really can, if that is what you wish.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to mention, I didn't refer to any of the names of the units involved, just to the form of the units.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not going into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. C-057, for having explained the composition of this unit to me, which was a battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to go into what you explained now during the private session, but during the introduction in one of these tabs - I think it was tab 13 - another thing was explained. This is an official information, I assume, of the security organs - I'm not going to read out the name of the security organ - which was submitted in connection with Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan. Observations. There is no doubt, evidently, that in this diagram that you provided his unit was within the composition of that battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, that is undoubted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Under the command of the battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in this information, on page 2, in paragraph 2, if we include the paragraph that started on the previous page, it says: "Arkan and his group consisting of about 25 to 30 men." So this well-known Serb Volunteer Guard, organised by Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan, then consisted of 25 to 30 men, and it is here together with the local Territorial Defence. It blended in with that unit. And both he and this Territorial Defence blended into this battalion under the command of that battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Tell me, please, this information that you referred to just now, what's its date? Just give me the date, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I cannot see it immediately. Oh, yes. The day is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Wait a moment for us all. We'll find the reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's tab 13. You can find it in the exhibit bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tab 13, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have pointed out that this was tab 13. And the date is the 1st of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right. I found the document myself now. The diagram that I explained to you a few minutes ago pertains to the 1st of November, which is a month later, and I think I said that a few minutes ago, that requests from that particular formation were not carried out and the guard was increased. At the moment that I'm talking about, the 1st of November, the guard had about 100 to 150 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how was it increased? People who were there in the Territorial Defence, they became part of the guard; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: No. The guard was increased -- well, actually, the people from the Territorial Defence did not join the guard or, rather, I don't know how it was increased. I just know that the members of the guard were significantly different from the JNA members and the members of the Territorial Defence. When we are talking about the 1st of November now. Each and every one of Arkan's men led a small group of local men. So they were all small-scale commanding officers, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they were integrated in the Territorial Defence as volunteers. They came there as volunteers and they were integrated into the Territorial Defence of that area, Eastern Slavonia; and the Territorial Defence itself, when this diagram was made, was subordinated to the command of your battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This can be seen from the diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That is what I wished to establish, because later, as far as I can see in the documents I have, this unit from the very outset joined the Territorial Defence in the area. Now, I think that we have gone through these exhibits, so I can make things easier both for myself and for you. Please, Mr. C-057, you know that my time is limited. Please try to be brief in your answers if you possibly can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Of course. I will try not to go into too much detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, that should be private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think when we go into details of the unit, there is a risk to reveal his identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's go on to something else or we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in paragraph 4, you say that there were a lot of Croats, so I will not go into that. You mention other ethnicities as well which I will not refer to lest I identify you. And in the same paragraph, if I understand this well, you say all ethnicities were represented and there was no intolerance on that ground, on that basis.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: If we are talking about paragraph 4, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And all this is true, accurate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Of course it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So there was no intolerance at that time, no inter-ethnic intolerance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: There was really none, at least not in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was a JNA unit which, as you say, was involved in JNA activities in Eastern Slavonia from the beginning of the war; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And when you say there was no intolerance, that implies all types of human relations in your unit, interpersonal relations in your unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, to the best of your knowledge and conviction, Mr. C-057, would it be fair to say that the JNA, at least in the time when you were in it and from what you know, in the battles in Eastern Slavonia acted as a genuinely Yugoslav army committed to Yugoslavia with a Yugoslav orientation that displayed no discrimination against any ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: I think it would be simplified to say so. It is true that my unit was mixed in terms of ethnicity, but it is also true that from the beginning of October nobody explained to us the objectives of our operation. Are we preserving Yugoslavia? Are we creating a Greater Serbia? Are we moving on to Zagreb? Nobody told us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you're answering to me only about your own unit, please limit yourself to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Nobody abandoned their position in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: The only person who did was a Serb of higher rank. He was the only one who left the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He was the only one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. And he was a Serb. And he did not run away because he was a nationalist but because he wanted to save his skin from this party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that major propaganda preceded this conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes, from the Croatian side. We were called the Serb-Chetnik army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you were referred to as the occupying force.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. I had occasion to listen to Radio Erdut myself where we were called "the Serb-Chetnik occupying army."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, since you are talking in the third paragraph about the fact that your unit was equipped, technically, 100 per cent, but the manpower level was only 30 to 40 per cent of establishment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-057
utterances.text: Yes. It was from April to the end of June 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are now going beyond the time and we have to adjourn. Witness C-057, I'm afraid we must ask you to come back next Tuesday to conclude your evidence, and I'm sorry we haven't been able to finish today, but we have to leave the courtroom because another case is going to come in. Mr. Milosevic, for your preparation, you can have one hour more of cross-examination of this witness on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just -- Your Honour, you have not reminded the witness yet that he is not to have contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff reminds me -- we haven't got an interpreter. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, would you remind the witness for me not to speak to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of December, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.05 p.m.,
